newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew up as Kleinwort rates "buy".
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew up as Kleinwort rates "buy".

text.p: Shares in Smith & Nephew Plc rose on Thursday, recovering from recent weakness as analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson issued a "buy" recommendation the day after S&N's demotion from the FTSE 100 index.
Analysts at Kleinwort noted that S&N shares were trading some 22 percent below their recent highs and that a lot of bad news had already been discounted.
"1997 will be a tough year but the worst is over," they said in a research note. "We only see upside from current levels."

The stock, which fell to a two-year low of 166-1/2p on May 21, was up 4p or 2.3 percent at 176 by 1036 GMT, among the strongest gainers in the FTSE 100 index. Volume reached an active 3.3 million shares.

Kleinwort said concern over the development of S&N's skin replacement Dermagraft should be eased after the first European launches this year. A review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration was expected sometime after the third quarter of the year.

Smith & Nephew's recent lacklustre share performance reduced its market value to a level where it was culled from the FTSE 100 index after Tuesday's close, along with retailer Burton Group Plc. Those two made way for former building societies Halifax and Alliance & Leicester.
S&N formally takes its leave from the FTSE 100 on June 23.
